How to use this very large guide

This is a very big guide. To make it easier, you can use the Quick start section if you want to quickly learn one of the inductions and the whole return sequence. Then, you can read the Let the next response guide you section, to learn what to do when your response is not guided by a recording. If you have questions, or want to learn more, there are lots of appendices, covering lots of topics, including questions, NLP patterns of language, working with anxiety, working with daydreams, altered states in general, what to do if you experience the sensation of a hostile presence, working with sleep, ways to influence others, and more inductions. The table of contents is hiding on the left

Introduction

Hello Lovey Bunny!

You are born with a full mind, a dreaming mind, protector, analyst, imitator, lover, remember, hider, revealor, healer etc…

You have never been taught how to live with all of those “layers” of yourself, and you were socialized with how to push, supress your emotions, pretend to be confident, have a good relationship with authority (or not), and so on and so forth. A lot of deep programs that all levels of your mind are running to help you navigate in the world, from your inner child to your inner guard, from your body to your intuition, from your fantasy to your “how to go throught my day manager”.

While many hypnosis teaching is about how to order your “subordinate” subconscious mind, I find much more interesting and rewarding to learn how to communicate well with all of them.

What we will do in that self hypnosis is prepare the ground and get the attention of all of them: your conscious mind, your subconscious mind, your body, your inner child, your inner protectors, your “adult”, your Higher Self, to have a meeting in your mind.

The method is pretty simple: we will learn to listen, warm them up, make them feel safe, ask for what we want clearly, test if it works in reality and act accordingly.

You don’t even need to go in some dramatic trance state, the only way to know if your new relationship with your whole mind is better is to test it in your life!

Let’s stop your conscious mind to talk like a crazy on the rooftop of your head and your subconscious mind to talk to you with “mysterious” signs like symptoms, dreams, crave, daydream, and other weird signals your body is throwing at you. Let’s make them talk like two adult human being! That’s communion!

I will make a lot of reference to your subconscious mind as if it was a rich ecology of “things” inside you, talk about Inner Child Reparenting, start from your Higher Self or the universal Love/Heart to get coherence in your mind, but also separate parts of you when needed, use prompt engineering and teach you how to be literate about influence as lots of things are hypnotizing you.
HG04-emuA:
Quick start: do this first

How does this work? In short: you gather your attention, you notice something, you do one thing in response, you wait, and you come all the way back out again. It’s a lot like playing or falling in love, or becoming curious, or gaining confidence. Nothing dramatic needs to happen.

Before you do your first session, read through the induction and full return while you’re awake. Find a time and a place where you will be physically secure for this time. Decide on one purpose for this session. Notice what you’re leaving alone for today. Put the screen aside and do the work.

As you do the induction, something will happen that you can notice: a sensation, an image, a phrase, a feeling, a “no way!” or a silence. Follow this guide for the next thing to do. This will vary based on what you need: warmth, a boundary, direction, time, and more. At the end of the session, come all the way back out, as described in this guide. Then write down what happened, and notice what you need to do in the “real world” to make this work.

If at any time you feel panicky, disoriented, unreal, or unable to function, the thing to do is come back out. This is not the same as noticing a bad feeling that you’ve chosen to experience, and being able to be with that feeling.

Do you usually think in words?

Before you pick a script, notice whether you have an inner voice. Do you notice words or phrases in your head, not spoken out loud, when you are thinking to yourself? All the time? Sometimes? Rarely? Almost never? (Note that the words do not have to be spoken aloud in your head. Just notice whether you use words when you think.) Does this vary depending on what kind of thinking you’re doing? Can you choose to think in words silently to yourself, even if you don’t usually do this?

This is different from noticing that in a particular situation, you notice feelings first and words later. It’s ok to say that you’re not sure; the point of these questions is to help you pick a way of doing this that will work for you, not to diagnose you.

If you don’t think in words, please read “say” and “ask” and “listen” in this guide as suggestions, not commands. You may want to say things out loud, or write them down, or use a recording, or just do the suggestion without wording it first. Also, do not assume that the child or protector needs to say things back to you in complete sentences. Nor does it mean that you will necessarily get an image instead; try things out and see what works.
HG12-emuA:
Why doing it myself worked better for me

Have I mentioned I'm a big fan of self-hypnosis? Doing it on my own seems far more useful than the very little I managed to do with a "professional". I'm sober right now, and I don't feel especially suggestible, but I suspect that's not even the main reason the pro didn't work very well for me.

When I do it on my own, I can detect when the wording I'm using for a suggestion to my subconscious is slightly off, and talk to my subconscious to find out what it thinks is wrong with the wording. When I use an image, I can tell whether it's giving me useful information, or just telling me what I'm afraid of, or what I want to avoid, or what I want to be true, or something else.

A hypnotist working on me can't interact with my subconscious mind quickly enough to get the detailed feedback needed to know what's going on in my mind, since he isn't IN my mind. (Of course, there are advantages to having someone else guiding the process, since they may be able to see things I'm blind to, and can help me keep the process regulated and safe.)

I found that especially amplified with loveyhuasca. My experiences included a much deeper understanding of my motivations, peaceful loving awareness operating alongside analytical clarity, the disappearance of unhelpful daydreaming, different priorities around relationships, stronger intuition, and repeated correction between intuition, subconscious response, and conscious analysis.

I also got stronger results when I practiced immediately after sky hypnosis:

Some benefits arrived the next morning or a few days later. After one loveyhuasca self-hypnosis session, I woke in what felt like an answer to prayer. I’d been dealing with a lot of lust energy and worrying it could pull me into a relationship that wasn’t right. I asked the subconscious to connect the heart chakra with the sacral chakra—to bring the love energy and sex energy into the same current. The next morning I woke in a kind of “perfected” love state. I didn’t feel that I needed to find a woman; the divine feminine felt somehow at zero distance from my heart. Ordinary interaction dissolved the state, but for a while it showed me a possibility my mind and heart may permit when the desire is sincere.

In the same vein, I was able to extend a short chrunga trip for what felt like a long time, and it feels like if I needed to I could have continued for an arbitrary amount of time. Only because of life did I have to talk to people, etc. Phenomenologically, this is very important. Although I don't recommend extending a trip, because it's better to integrate, etc.

This probably works for non-drug induced self hypnosis too - or meditation, but for that I find it works way better in a lucid dream - explained in the lucid dreaming guide .
HG15-emuA:
When “your voice” is everybody else’s voice

Working with your inner child can be harder when you did not have a private self to begin with. This happens a lot when people come from a background where their family, religion or community took over their life very early on, or they were pressured to achieve in a certain way at a young age. This means that you don’t know who you are, what you feel, what you want, what you believe, what you like, or what you don’t like until you hear what someone else says first. This makes it hard to follow the advice to “love yourself” when you don’t know who “yourself” is. So in these cases, reparenting needs to go hand in hand with finding yourself. For some, it’s easy to work with their child-self because they can feel their child-self really easily. For others, it requires creating safety and playing around more to feel their child-self.

You might be in this camp if:

You don’t know what you want until you hear what someone else wants

You find that your opinions change dramatically depending on who is around

You catch yourself agreeing with someone when you didn’t agree in the moment

You tend to take responsibility for other people’s emotions to the detriment of yourself

Trying to love yourself feels like a performance

Trying to find out how your inner child feels, results in guesses instead of feeling

You find that you can rebel, but you can’t choose

The reason for this is that a part of your brain didn’t have the opportunity to explore “what do I like?” and “what do I want to try out?” because as a child you were focused on finding ways not to hurt yourself or lose attachment.

Sometimes it is necessary to distance yourself for a certain period from the people or group that you are getting your answers from so that you can distinguish between what you want and what you are told to want. However, you don’t need to do this for long – just long enough to differentiate what is yours from what is social.

This means moving from a “human doer” to a “human being”. If you don’t feel like you are good enough just because you exist, you will try to create a sense of worth by being beautiful, by doing something well, by being smart, by gaining status, by being more spiritual than everyone else, or by being needed. In all of these cases, you are essentially making a bargain with yourself – that as long as you are good at something (or good at being good for other people), you will be good enough to belong. And if you fall short in that arena, you feel that you are not good enough.

To help you find yourself, ask yourself these questions:

What do I like when no one is watching?

What do I believe before I check what other people think?

What do I want that is not in rebellion to others, and is not in compliance with others?

Where am I buying my sense of belonging by betraying myself?

What “arena” am I using to try to buy my sense of belonging?

What can I try on for size that I don’t need to impress anyone with?

What relationships allow me to be myself?

What do I notice in my body and what meaning am I attaching to it?

Remember that your inner child needs to play! Try out some things that have no value towards your resume – painting, dancing, gardening, learning a language, a sport, volunteering, playing music, etc. Your parent may be telling you that you are supposed to be good at something as soon as you start doing it. Your job as your own parent is to remind yourself that you are not doing these things to prove your worth – you are doing them to see if you like them or not. And it will take some time before the humiliation of being a beginner goes away.

As a child, belonging was essential to your survival. As an adult, it can manifest in families, religions, romantic relationships, political tribes, spiritual groups, institutions, or even online. Part of “adulting” is finding out where you are trading your sense of self in exchange for belonging, and then consciously choosing where you want to belong – on your terms. A large part of your subconscious mind is made up of the voices of other people, so this is also a good opportunity to use some of the tools in this self-hypnosis guide to help you let go of them.

Where am I betraying myself in exchange for belonging?

What would it feel like to belong without having to betray myself?

Is this my own guidance or a belonging program I adopted?

Is this love, or is it a fear of being excluded?

Is this my conscience or is it conditioning?

Is this devotion, or is it compliance?

Is this rebellion, or is it freedom?

Then see what your body tells you.
HG16-emuA:
De-hypnosis: wake up inside the influence

One of the best side-effects of learning self-hypnosis is an increased awareness of all the ways you’re being manipulated in your day-to-day life. By a screen? By a specific ad? By a politician? By a religion? By erotic imprinting? By an authority figure? By the desire for belonging? By shame? By a sense of urgency? By repetition? It’s all around you. Sometimes it’s benign – like lullabies or prayers or being taught by a good teacher or listening to a beautiful song or being in love. But you may want to ask yourself what effect it’s having on your ability to see clearly and make choices.

Some common ways you may know you’re being manipulated include a sense of urgency, a sense of specialness, FOMO, being made to feel like you won’t be included if you don’t go along, sexual charge, shame, being confused, a fantasy of being rescued, a sense of destiny, a sense that you should obey, a sense of secret knowledge, or an excessive sense of certainty about something pretty quickly.

If you’re being hypnotically influenced, stop. Don’t listen. Don’t rebel, either, just stop and realize that you’re being influenced.

Some common ways hypnotic language becomes manipulative includes:

“you’ll realize, eventually, that…” “you may eventually admit that…” “the reason you’re not feeling it yet is…” “even if part of you doesn’t feel that’s true…” “your higher self knows…” “everyone knows…” “the reason you don’t believe that’s true is your ego’s fear of…”

Other language patterns to watch out for include:

Is it telling you what you’re going to do or experience? Is there an implied lack of choice? Is it presupposing things that may not be true? Who benefits from you being in this frame of mind? Is it ramping up emotions that aren’t serving you? Is it not giving you information you should have? Can you easily say “no” without there being consequences (shame, getting mocked, not being let into the group, being labeled “unspiritual,” etc.)?

Even a good guide should be helping you to bring your adult self into the experience more. The more powerful the state, the more you should have boundaries.

Soft language can still take away choice

Language that’s permissive but that still takes your choice away includes:

Utilizing indirect patterns, which often work better because they bypass the conscious mind, but can be specific about where they’re going even if vague in their language, may just seem conversational, or use suggestions.

Using induction patterns while seeming to “explain” things (even some of my explanations of how to avoid hypnosis use some of the mechanics of induction).

Setting it up so that any response the listener gives is compliance (answering “yes” or “no,” noticing something, not noticing something, resisting, not responding).

Using bind patterns (“whether or not you notice…”).

Telling you who you are or using language that makes you feel like you “belong” to the guide or that being “good” or “safe” comes from obeying the guide or a role.

Fractionating you without telling you they’re doing it.

Using post-session cues (gestures, blinks, sounds, even having you listen to something more than once) that they haven’t told you about that will make you do something later.

Making you forget things, telling you something is true, utilizing “dream logic,” utilizing imagery or body sensations to make you believe something is true.

Not actually letting you “out” at the end of the recording, leaving you in a role, or leaving you in a state where your ability to use good judgment or move your body is impaired or leaving you blank or in an altered state for an indefinite amount of time.

Make sure you have a real choice to not proceed with the induction at any time, make it more gentle, use a different way, not be in an altered state at all, or stop or pause the induction and know that “no” really means “no.” Even not responding or not being sure should not be taken for “yes” just because someone’s voice sounds nice.

For a longer de-hypnosis checklist, see Appendix C.
HG18-emuA:
Come all the way back

Come out of the session by reversing the entry method; if you floated, come back down by the same method; land with your chosen weight. If you shrunk, come back to your normal size. If you meet your younger self or parts, make sure that you acknowledge that you are now whole, this is your body, and you are using your adult judgement. If you traveled, then come back the same way you left. Make sure that you are only bringing back what you had intended to bring back.

You may wish to say, “I am bringing back only that which I choose to bring back at this time. All that is not needed at this time will remain safely stored away until such time as I am ready. I am now coming back to this place and to my body and to normal day to day living. All instructions given to me in this session are now over except for the conscious intention (or cue) to implement in the future.”

Count yourself out: 1. Coming back into your body and your chosen weight. 2. Coming back to your normal breathing pattern. 3. Coming back to awareness of your surroundings and of your location. 4. Moving your fingers and your toes and your shoulders and your eyes. 5. Opening your eyes, feeling present, normal and clear. Your session is now over.

It is a good idea to say to yourself what day it is or what the date is, look to your left and to your right, look at something near and something far away, move about a bit before you stand up, stand up and make sure that you are oriented and alert. Take note of anything that came up during your session and what you may or may not need to do as a result, and then just go about doing something normal.

In the event that a recording that you are listening to stops unexpectedly, simply say to yourself “the recording has stopped and the session is over” and then use the above method to come out by opening your eyes, saying where you are, saying what day it is, pushing down with your feet or your hands, moving about, looking around and then using the 5 step method.

Note: If you are using a recording to go to sleep, then it is all right to let the recording put you to sleep or have you in a quiet resting state. However, if you are waking when the recording ends, then it should not leave you in any state that is not conducive to normal functioning, such as leaving you in a role, with lowered judgement, impaired movement capabilities, blank or with an undefined reset word, etc.
HG19-emuA:
The actual inner meeting

Make sure you are not lying down when you do this exercise, unless you are ready to go to sleep or receive deep rest or are trying to incubate dreams. Sit in a place where you will not find yourself daydreaming, dissociating or going to sleep. Keep your spine straight, but not rigid, like a soldier. Relax your jaw and maintain some connection with the room you are in.

You can say to yourself, “I’m not going to leave life, I’m just going to listen more deeply to life.”

Invoking: “With the help of my Higher Self, my universal heart-mind connection, my wise subconscious mind, the intelligence in my body, my inner child, my inner adults, my protective parts and everyone and everything else that can help me to know what I need to know, only what I need to know in a useful, kind, stabilizing, real way…

Ask your conscious mind to listen.

This doesn’t mean you have to silence your thoughts to listen. Notice your thoughts, sensations, images, doubts, emotions, etc., without fighting them, without going with them, but simply noticing them while you hold the intention of this exercise in the background of your mind. Notice what becomes salient to you.

You can say, “Tell me what I need to know or tell me what I need to know to ask, and I will sit in silence for five minutes and listen.”

You might hear a phrase, feel a sensation, notice a memory, see a color, be contacted by a child or protector, feel pain, warmth, silence or know that your need to do something or be grateful for something or that this is enough listening for today.

Listen to it all and believe none of it.
HG21-emuA:
The 15-minute daily practice

You may choose to do all of this practice, or learn the second script. Either way, you'll be using a similar process and can use these recordings as a base for your own practice. These exercises only need to be done for fifteen minutes or so. This is not a therapeutic time, but merely enough time to induce yourself (a few minutes), do what you are going to do (in this case 5 minutes of sitting in silence and listening), and then bring yourself back out again (a few minutes). You can break out of the process at any time, if you feel you need to do something else.

B) Notice three things you can see, then three things you can hear and three sensations you can feel in your body. Now do two of each, then one of each. Count from 5 to 1 and start listening.

After practicing a few times with these scripts, feel free to edit them down and remove any parts that you feel are no longer necessary to help you induce yourself. The idea is that eventually, you will not even need to play them back. But there is no harm in using them if you enjoy it. (Note: in script A, the part about coming back out again is optional; if you are familiar with the induction process, it will probably be enough to simply count).

When you come out of the process, consider whether there is anything you would like to nurture with more warmth, or protect, or direct in a way that moves it in the direction of truth and love and life. Perhaps there is something you would like to explore or build up. You may want to take this process with you as you move about your day. If there is something you need to do, then make a plan with yourself to do that thing. Be concrete and say something like, "If _________ , then I will do________ ." Then see how things are later on: how you are sleeping, relating and functioning.
HG23-emuA:
Capacity before content

NOTE: If it is medically unsafe for you to do this, or you are panicking, sleep deprived, nauseated, deeply destabilized, manic, in a psychosis-like state, or overwhelmed by chemicals, please stabilize first before seeking out what your subconscious needs you to know. It is not ready for you to know it if it requires you to destabilize to know it!

There are times when your subconscious seems to know something that it is difficult for your conscious mind to know. It may be about your sexuality, a grief, trauma, your family, betrayal, shame, vocation, a relationship, fears about illness, spirituality, an addiction, your identity, or a moral issue.

What you don’t want to do is bully your subconscious with statements like,

“Why don’t you just tell me?” “What are you hiding?” “Tell me right now!” or “I demand that you reveal the truth!”

This can lead to flooding, panic, false certainty, confabulation, dissociation, and just generally making your day suck more. When you’re flooded, it can be hard to access your adult capacities to pause, choose, reality test, plan and make choices for yourself. Until your adult has enough of these capacities, especially regulation and support, it is not good for your subconscious to communicate with you. Silence is safer. But when your adult does have enough regulation, support, humility, and other capacities, you can talk with your subconscious.

“What do you need for my conscious mind to be able to know what you’re saying 5% better?” “Can you tell me through a symbol?” “Can you tell me what you need me to do to be safe without telling me what it is?” “Do you need me to get support to be able to know what it is? Who?”

You may even want to say, “Dear wise subconscious mind, if there is something you know that my conscious mind can’t handle, please don’t just break it open in a way that isn’t good for me. Please prepare me to hear it in a way that is safe. Ground me. Get me support. Tell me what to do.”

REMEMBER: Hypnotic imagery is not always literal, especially around trauma and memory.
HG25-emuA:
What not to do

DO NOT: See the voices, images, movements or body signals as real, but always reality test them.

DO NOT obsess about “downloading” grandiose information or become obsessed with demons, jinn, “Unattached Burdens”, etc. Stabilize yourself. Get help if necessary, especially if not reality testing well or if not functioning well in life.

DO NOT do self-hypnosis while driving a car, bathing, swimming, or otherwise doing something that requires active participation.

DO NOT try to “force” memories to “prove” something to yourself or ignore medical symptoms by “forcing” them down through hypnosis.

DO NOT “force” yourself to ignore basic body signals, like hunger, tiredness, pain, etc., or basic emotions, like grief, anger, fear, etc.

DO NOT “extend” altered states indefinitely or take intuitive hits as “real” without reality testing them.

DO NOT allow any inner state, like the “Inner Child” or “Protector” or “Nurturer” or “Leader” to take over completely. They each need the others.

DO NOT use NLP techniques to “force” down “protectors” or to do anything else that does not make logical sense, like to manipulate people or to “heal” something that the body is saying cannot be healed.

Don’t convince yourself that negative indicators like doubt, distraction, resistance, or lack of response, or saying “No” are good indicators that the induction is working.

Don’t rely solely upon the “safety” of “the unconscious mind”. Always make certain that the circumstances are as safe as possible and that there is a safe way out.

Don’t believe that normal physical sensations are indicators of trauma, illness, body toxins, demonic possession, “attachments”, “transformations” or anything else, just because the “subconscious” says they are.

Don’t believe that anything is “healed” physically or neurologically/cellularly, simply because it is “healed” in the imagination.

Don’t ever allow anyone to put “commands” in without giving them to yourself consciously and knowing why and wanting them, so that they can be used repeatedly and reviewed and removed if they are no longer wanted. There is no way to “put something in” that cannot be removed, but saying “I remove them” may not be enough. Don’t allow anyone to give commands to someone else to give to “YOU” or to make YOU do anything or change to a different person or have amnesia, etc.

DO bring yourself back to normal consciousness as yourself at the end of each session while awake.
HG26-emuA:
When this needs more support than a guide can provide

Self-hypnosis is a relationship you have with yourself, and sometimes the situation calls for more than that.

Get urgent help now if you’re confused, in danger, or experiencing physical symptoms like chest pain or fainting. If you’re experiencing new or worsening suicidal thoughts, severe insomnia, or symptoms of mania or psychosis, or if your dissociative symptoms are impacting your functioning, please get help for those promptly, rather than trying to fix them with this 4- to 12-week practice.

On the other hand, you may need very little more support. Start small—do shorter practices, make them warm, choose a small and tractable subject to work with, make sure you’re coming all the way back out of hypnosis, and track the effect on one target area (anxiety, chronic daydreaming, repairing a relationship, getting something done, sleep, emotional regulation, intuitive accuracy, etc.) for a week or two. If you find that your functioning worsens or you’re gaining certainty about something that can’t be verified, then it may be time to reassess.

Get some other appropriate help if you’re dealing with recurring panic attacks, compulsive behaviors, substance-related destabilization, or major relationship instability.

Methods to explore with a trained person present

If you want to deliberately use regression to explore the origins of a traumatic experience that you don’t know, to follow an affect or somatic bridge to unknown traumatic origins, or if you expect substantial flashback or dissociative reactions, work with a trauma-informed trained clinician who is trained in the method you’re using and who is present while you do it. (Affect and somatic bridges mean following associations from an emotional or bodily feeling; regression means remembering or imagining what it would have been like when you were younger. Both can also be used for more stable purposes, like finding resources.) Even if you work with a clinician, please note that hypnosis can’t prove what did or didn’t happen in your life.

Having a history of trauma, crying when you access inner children, or even wanting to feel difficult feelings, doesn’t necessarily mean you need more support than working on your own. It is up to you to find how wide or narrow a range to work in, and that will be different for different people.

Most guidelines for treating major trauma recommend some variant of trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy, such as cognitive processing therapy, prolonged exposure, or eye movement desensitization and reprocessing. Self-hypnosis and inner child work can be part of that process. If you’re working with high-risk trauma, you may want a bigger container for that work.

The ultimate feedback on whether your process is working well is how you’re functioning in ordinary life. If you’re being more loving, honest, functional, relational, grounded, and precise than you were before you started, then keep doing what you’re doing. If you’re functioning less well than before, then stop trying to go deeper and focus instead on getting enough sleep, eating, grounding yourself, maintaining healthy boundaries with others, and getting support from others.
HG28-emuA:
Try it in the Inner Signal app

Welcome to Inner Signal, the app designed to help you take your first steps into the world of hypnosis. Here you’ll find several voice-recorded sessions to guide you, information about the method you’re using, and tips on how to develop your own language for hypnotic self-talk. After each session, you’ll have the chance to report what went through your mind and body, and consider what you might have missed, so you can learn to catch more of your inner experience next time. You can also ask the app questions about how a hypnotherapist might approach particular issues. You don’t need an app to do self-hypnosis, and you don’t have to graduate from this app before looking for a practitioner to work with, but it may help to have a starting point.

If you’re using the ChatGPT version of this app, you might want to upload a picture, drawing, poem or song to talk about instead of writing out your explanation in prose. But please make sure the file you upload can be seen or heard by the chat you’re currently using! It will probably tell you that it can’t see or hear the file if you’ve made this mistake. Please remember that what you say about what’s in the file, what it means to you, and what the app thinks it means, are three different things, and that you get to decide for yourself whether the app has interpreted it correctly – you don’t have to defend your choice of medium.

Bear in mind that even with its voice recordings, the app is asking you what’s going on for you – it can’t feel it in its own body, like a trained practitioner might be able to do. The app is not pretending to be a skilled therapist, just helping you to learn for yourself, so that you can make informed choices about what to try next.

Always enter this app via this page, not by bookmarking the app itself, to make sure you get the current version.

Please fill in this survey with what you’ve learned from using the app, so that you have something to analyse later, and others can benefit from what you’ve experienced.

If you have any real questions about what the app has said, or if there’s something you want to ask that it doesn’t answer, please contact me here to discuss arranging a consultation.
HG29+30-emuA:
Appendices

You can ignore everything below if you just stay on the main path. Everything below is a possible addition to make the process more precise or safer. It is mainly for special situations and there are scripts you can use.

Appendix A: How to ask the subconscious a useful question

Your subconscious is not an AI but some things are transferable. You need to make sure that prompt engineering serves you to be more present, more honest, more loving and hear the messages of your subconscious better.

The following elements can be relevant for prompt engineering when you need to be more precise:

Role: Who is it that you talk to

Context: Which situation is it

Intention: What do you want to achieve

Constraint: What constraints do you want to set to make it more safe or to be more precise (like do not force things, be truthful, be loving etc.)

Output: Which kind of output is most helpful for you? Images, words, signals in your body, memories, next actions, questions, symbols etc. Or sometimes it is best to simply rest.

Evaluation: How will you know if you got a good answer? Criteria like is it true, kind, timely, brings stability, specific, testable etc.

Iteration: Change the prompt depending on the feedback you get from life

In some prompts it is good to include that it is safe for the system to not give an answer. Otherwise your analytical brain will feel like it needs to come up with something and distort things.

Sometimes there is simply nothing going on or the answer is that it is not the right time and you should rest and build up capacity or do the obvious things you know you need to do.

Appendix E: Is the daydream helping or replacing your life?

Sometimes, daydreaming is intuitive. Your subconscious is simulating an idea or event to help you digest trauma or teach you something. The act of daydreaming may also be a creative exercise or a way your subconscious is telling you about the future. Sometimes your subconscious will show you things you’re afraid of, so you can learn to deal with them. Sometimes it shows you what you want.

Other times, it’s a detriment. An escape from reality. An addiction to fantasy rather than reality. Dissociation from the pain of real life. Obsession with romantic partners. Refusal to accept the responsibilities of adult life.

How do you know which one it is? Ask yourself, “Is my daydreaming bringing me back into life or taking me away from it?”

If it’s helping you, ask for more specific guidance.

If it’s taking you away from life, immediately sit up straight and open your eyes. Then ask your subconscious for help. “Hey subconscious, thanks for all these interesting images. If they’re helpful, please show me what I need to know. If they’re just a way for me to avoid dealing with life, please bring me into the present and show me how to deal with life in a gentle but structured way.”

Then ask yourself, “What do I need to do in the real world that I’m avoiding by daydreaming?”

It could be anything from “send a text message” or “stop sending text messages” to “clean my room” or “eat” or “sleep” or “deal with my grief” or “create something” or “apologize” or “leave someone” or “tell the truth” or “make a plan” or “get help” or “return to the task at hand” or “stop fantasizing about people who can’t love me.”

Appendix G: Altered states

Mind Altered States & Inner Child Work Note: I am NOT encouraging anyone to use these. However, many people do attempt their first self-hypnosis, contact with their inner child or contact with their Higher Self while in a mind altered state.

If you choose to do so, please be aware that you should not use this state to force open anything, but rather use it to enhance your ability to love and improve your life.

Many people have opened to certain things in their life in altered states. The key is that though it is great that this opened, it is different to have had the experience of love, to be able to access it in a particular state and to be able to access it on a day to day basis. Sometimes if the child can't take it, you may need to open the experience up a bit more.

So if you are in an altered state, rather than asking for a revelation, you may want to use these phrases: Help me to ground. Help me to only take that which I can integrate. Help me to remember the love I am feeling. Help me to come back again when the time is right. Help me to take something from this and change my regular life.

You should not use self-hypnosis to keep you in an altered state forever, to help you remember things, to make you more afraid, to help you not sleep, to not see a doctor, or to not communicate with other people.

If you find that being in an altered state is helping you to love less, to be more ungrounded, to be less honest, to not sleep, to not communicate or to not do regular life things, then you should stop attempting to go deeper and instead work on integrating what you have.

Stabilize before you interpret

Self-hypnosis can be extremely powerful when used in altered states of consciousness such as when one is loveyhuasca, meditating, in a lucid dream, grieving, utilizing sexual energy, praying, not sleeping, or in other states similar to plant medicines.

The problem is that people think that because they are in an altered state, that it must mean something. Sometimes it is your inner child talking, sometimes it is a Protector scaring you, and sometimes it is shame/grief/anger or other parts coming out, but often it is simply your body being overloaded by the experience, the chaos of the environment, lack of sleep, or some other reason that it just doesn't make sense. Just because you had a picture that scared you doesn't mean it's true, just because you had a bad feeling doesn't mean it's helpful and just because you had a download in a nice lighting doesn't mean you should believe it.

Before trying to interpret what is happening in an altered state, you should

“What kind of problem is happening?”
